text.p: Following is the text of a statement issued by the Indian Finance Ministry on Tuesday announcing the introduction of 14-day auction treasury bills:
"With a view to providing investors with instrument of varying short-term maturities, Government has decided to introduce the auction of 14-day Treasury Bills.

The salient feature of the 14-day Auction Treasury Bills are: 1.The 14-day Auction Treasury Bills would be issued and repaid only at Mumbai (Bombay). The Reserve Bank would issue from time to time press releases indicating particulars on the date of auction, announcement of results and the date for making payments.
2. There will be no notified amount for auctions.

3.The Bills may be purchased by any person resident in India including individuals, firms, companies, corporate bodies and institutions. State governments, eligible Provident Funds and the Nepal Rastra Bank will be allowed to bid in auction on non-competitive basis.

4. The Bills will be issued for a minimum amount of 25,000 rupees and multiples thereof. The bill would be issued at a discounted price. The minimum offer price (cut-off price) above which bids will be accepted will be announced on the day of the auction.
5. The bills would form part of the borrowings of Government of India.
6. The Bills would an approved investment for SLR (statutory liquidity ratio) purposes."
